newsitem.title: USA: CBOT panel predicts soy price gains on USDA stocks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT panel predicts soy price gains on USDA stocks.

text.p: A Chicago Board of Trade-sponsored panel of analysts agreed CBOT soybean futures should climb further due to a cut by the government in its outlook for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks.
"It's a somewhat friendly report paced by the soy complex with the carryout cut to 140 million bushels," said Robert Lekberg, grain analyst for Chicago-based trade house Goldenberg, Hehmeyer and Co.
The U.S. Agriculture Department's February Supply/Demand Report released early Wednesday pegged 1996-97 U.S. soybean carryout at 140 million bushels.
The projection was below the 155 million bushel tally predicted by the USDA in its January supply/demand data.
CBOT traders said soybean futures Wednesday should open from three to five cents per bushel higher.
Mickey Luth, Chicago-based director of research for LaiFa Group said the soybean carryout number could be further reduced in future USDA reports.
"Demand is outstanding around the world, initially led by China and now by European demand," Luth said.
Luth told a press conference his prediction for soybean carryover could fall to 116 million bushels.

Luth and Lekberg said USDA's forecast for Brazilian soybean production this year at 26.5 million tonnes and Argentina's at 13.5 million tonnes were about as expected and should have no significant impact on soybean futures.
In January, USDA pegged the Brazilian crop at 26 million and Argentina's at 13 million tonnes.

They said corn futures could find mild support from the USDA report which left unchanged the 1996-97 corn carryout at 959 million bushels. CBOT corn futures early Wednesday were called to open one to two cents per bushel higher.
"It's a little bit friendly relative to the fact USDA didn't kick up the carryover as some had expected," Lekberg said.
There also were no surprises in the government's balance sheet for wheat, the analysts said. CBOT wheat futures were called to open two to three cents higher.
USDA increased slightly its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryout to 474 million tonnes, above the January forecast for 469 million.
Wheat futures surged in late dealings Tuesday amid news of mounting Canadian transportation problems.
"The Canadian logistics problem is giving the market a boost here," Luth said. "But this is one of those rallies that's temporary and we'll go back to test contract lows."
